title: Best YouTube Thumbnail Designers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a YouTube thumbnail designer: what the package should include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags.
intro: A thumbnail is often the only thing a viewer sees before deciding whether to click, and it has to work at the size of a fingernail on a phone screen. Most weak thumbnails try to say too much or use images the creator has no right to use. This guide shows you how to order thumbnails that are clear, honest and yours.

faq.q: What size should a YouTube thumbnail be?
faq.a: Ask for a 16:9 image at a high resolution, within the file size limit YouTube shows when you upload. Also ask the designer to check it at small sizes, because most viewers see it tiny on a phone.

faq.q: Should I send my own photos?
faq.a: If your face or product appears, yes. Send sharp, well-lit photos with clear expressions. Your own photos avoid copyright problems and make the thumbnail feel like your channel.

faq.q: Can I get the editable file?
faq.a: Ask for it. A layered file, such as a PSD or a template in a design tool, lets you change the text or reuse the layout for later videos without ordering again.

faq.q: How many versions should I order?
faq.a: Two or three versions of the same video's thumbnail let you compare. YouTube Studio may offer a test-and-compare feature for thumbnails on eligible channels, which makes extra versions more useful.

faq.q: Can the designer use images from movies, games or other creators?
faq.a: Be careful. Screenshots and photos you do not own can lead to copyright claims. Use your own footage and photos, licensed stock images, or artwork made for you.
